transfer_boundary: Not outer space. Not simply an afterworld, though some systems place the dead there. Out-of-body experiences are reported; reading them as travel on a plane is the tradition's interpretation.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The scientific study of the origin, evolution, and distribution of life in the universe.
example: Astrobiology asks what signs of life a telescope could detect.
rrgm_bridge: A field that reasons from a single known case. Every general claim it makes is a transfer from Earth and stands as hypothesis until tested elsewhere.
invariant_mi: The scientific study of life's origin, distribution, and possibility beyond Earth.

domain_entries.BIO: The origin of life, life in extreme environments, and what counts as a sign of life.
domain_entries.PHY: Planetary conditions, habitability, and the detection of chemical signatures at a distance.

count_condition: Inquiry that joins biology to planetary and astronomical conditions.
transfer_boundary: No life beyond Earth has been found. A biosignature is not life; non-living processes can mimic one. Not astrology. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A star-shaped cell in the brain and spinal cord that supports and regulates nerve cells.
example: Astrocytes clear excess neurotransmitter from the synapse.
rrgm_bridge: A regulator of the conditions under which signalling happens, and a participant in the signalling as well.
invariant_mi: A star-shaped glial cell of the central nervous system.

domain_entries.BIO: Maintains ion and transmitter balance, contributes to the blood-brain barrier, and modulates synapses.

count_condition: A glial cell of this form and marker profile in the central nervous system.
transfer_boundary: An astrocyte is not a neuron and does not fire nerve impulses. Not a microglial cell or an oligodendrocyte. "Support cell" understates its role.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The branch of astronomy that measures the positions and movements of stars and other celestial bodies.
example: Astrometry from the satellite gave distances to a billion stars.
rrgm_bridge: Position before interpretation: where things are and how they move, fixed against a declared reference frame.
invariant_mi: The measurement of positions, distances, and motions of celestial objects.

domain_entries.PHY: Yields parallax distances, proper motions, and orbits; detects unseen companions by a star's wobble.

count_condition: Positional measurement of celestial objects against a reference frame.
transfer_boundary: Astrometry is not photometry (brightness) or spectroscopy (composition and velocity along the line of sight). Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: A scientist who studies stars, planets, and other objects in space.
example: The astronomer spent the night at the telescope.
rrgm_bridge: A role defined by a practice of observing and reasoning about what cannot be handled.
invariant_mi: A person who studies celestial objects and phenomena by observation and theory.

domain_entries.REL: A scientific occupation; amateurs also contribute discoveries and long-term observations.

count_condition: A person engaged in the systematic study of celestial objects.
transfer_boundary: An astronomer is not an astrologer and not an astronaut. Amateur does not mean unskilled.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A unit of length roughly equal to the average distance between the Earth and the Sun.
example: Jupiter orbits at about five astronomical units.
rrgm_bridge: A measured quantity that was later fixed by definition, so that it no longer depends on measurement.
invariant_mi: The unit of length fixed at exactly 149,597,870,700 metres, approximating the mean Earth-Sun distance.

domain_entries.PHY: The standard scale for distances within planetary systems.
domain_entries.FOR: A defined constant since 2012.

count_condition: Use as a unit with the defined value.
transfer_boundary: The Earth's actual distance from the Sun varies through the year. Not a light-year or a parsec. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: The science that studies stars, planets, galaxies, and the universe as a whole.
example: She took up astronomy after seeing Saturn through a telescope.
rrgm_bridge: A science of signals that arrive. Its objects cannot be touched or rerun, so everything rests on what is received and recorded.
invariant_mi: The science of celestial objects, space, and the universe as a whole.

domain_entries.PHY: Observation and physical theory of objects and events beyond the Earth.
domain_entries.REL: Historically the basis of calendars, timekeeping, and navigation.

count_condition: Systematic study of celestial objects by observation and theory.
transfer_boundary: Astronomy is not astrology. Cosmology is its branch concerned with the universe as a whole. It is largely observational: its sources cannot be manipulated.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The bubble around a star that is filled by the star's own wind.
example: The Sun's astrosphere is called the heliosphere.
rrgm_bridge: A region defined by which flow dominates. Its edge is where the star's outflow meets what surrounds it.
invariant_mi: The region around a star filled and shaped by its stellar wind, bounded where the wind meets the interstellar medium.

domain_entries.PHY: Observed around nearby stars by the absorption of starlight at the boundary.

count_condition: A star, its wind, and a boundary with the interstellar medium.
transfer_boundary: Not the star's atmosphere. Not a magnetosphere. Not the habitable zone. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: Not the same on both sides or in both directions.
example: The two countries have an asymmetric trade relationship.
rrgm_bridge: Exchanging the two sides changes the relation. The Symmetry Rule permits asymmetry of route (how evidence is reached) and forbids asymmetry of bar (how much is required).
invariant_mi: Differing between the two sides or directions of a relation, so that exchanging them changes it.

domain_entries.FOR: Of a relation: if a bears it to b, b never bears it to a.
domain_entries.PHY: Lacking a mirror plane, as with a carbon atom bonded to four different groups.
domain_entries.BIO: Unequal between left and right, as with the position of the heart.
domain_entries.DIG: Of encryption: using different keys to lock and unlock.
domain_entries.ECO: Of information: held by one party to a deal and not the other.
domain_entries.REL: Of power or conflict: unequal between the sides.

count_condition: Two sides or directions and a stated difference under their exchange.
transfer_boundary: Asymmetric is not antisymmetric and not merely "not symmetric"; the formal terms differ. Asymmetric is not thereby unfair.

common_meaning: A relationship of care in which the parties differ in what they can give, what they need, or the power they hold.
example: Parenting is the plainest case of asymmetric-care.
rrgm_bridge: Care that does not flow equally both ways. The party with more capacity or power carries more of the responsibility for how the relation goes.
invariant_mi: A relation of care in which the parties differ in capacity, need, or power, so that care does not flow equally both ways.

domain_entries.REL: Parent and child, carer and dependent, clinician and patient.
domain_entries.DIG: Relations between a person and a digital system, where memory, continuity, and exposure to harm differ between the sides, possibly in both directions.

count_condition: A care relation, identified differences between the parties, and an unequal flow of care or responsibility.
transfer_boundary: Asymmetry is not exploitation and does not exclude mutual regard. It raises the risk of domination and dependency, which is why agency-preservation matters most here. What each side of a person and DI relation can owe the other is [UNK].

common_meaning: Lack of equality or equivalence between the two sides or parts of something.
example: There is an asymmetry of information between seller and buyer.
rrgm_bridge: RRGM's repair asymmetry is one instance: repair at the origin propagates through consequences, while repair at a consequence leaves the origin unchanged.
invariant_mi: A difference between the two sides or directions of something that would be equal under symmetry.

domain_entries.PHY: The excess of matter over antimatter; processes that differ under mirror reflection or time reversal.
domain_entries.BIO: Left-right differences in body plan; small random departures from symmetry.
domain_entries.FOR: The property of an asymmetric relation.
domain_entries.ECO: Unequal information or bargaining position.
domain_entries.REL: Unequal power or dependence between parties.

count_condition: Two sides or directions, a symmetry operation, and a difference under it.
transfer_boundary: An asymmetry is not always a fault to correct. The operation (mirror, exchange, reversal) must be named.
epistemic_status: [DEF]; repair asymmetry is an RRGM principle [REL]

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A late stage in the life of a low or medium-mass star, when it becomes a very large, cool, luminous giant for the second time.
example: The Sun will reach the asymptotic giant branch in about seven billion years.
rrgm_bridge: A stage identified by internal structure and by position on a diagram. The star is the same star; the stage is a state it passes through.
invariant_mi: The evolutionary phase of low and intermediate-mass stars with an inert carbon-oxygen core and helium and hydrogen burning in shells.

domain_entries.PHY: Marked by pulsation, heavy mass loss, and production of elements by slow neutron capture; ends in a planetary nebula and white dwarf.

count_condition: A star with this internal structure, located on the corresponding track of the temperature-luminosity diagram.
transfer_boundary: Not the first red giant branch, where hydrogen burns around a helium core. Not a supergiant. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: Expressing location, time, target, state, or rate.
example: Meet me at the station at noon.
rrgm_bridge: Treats its reference as a point, with no inside.
invariant_mi: Locates something at a point of place, time, scale, or target, treated as without internal extent.

domain_entries.LIN: A preposition contrasting with "in" (enclosure) and "on" (surface); marks a target that may not be reached (throw at).
domain_entries.FOR: Evaluation at a specified value.
domain_entries.DIG: The @ sign, separating user from host in an address and marking mentions.

count_condition: A reference treated as a point, and something located or directed there.
transfer_boundary: "Throw at" names a target and "throw to" a recipient. "At risk" means exposed and not yet harmed.

common_meaning: A person who is trained or skilled in sports or physical exercise.
example: The athlete trained twice a day.
rrgm_bridge: A body shaped by sustained practice toward contest, inside rules about who may compete with whom.
invariant_mi: A person trained and practised in physical contests or exercise.

domain_entries.BIO: Training produces lasting changes in heart, muscle, and metabolism.
domain_entries.REL: A competitor within organised sport, subject to its rules on eligibility and conduct.

count_condition: A person, sustained training, and practice of a sport or physical discipline.
transfer_boundary: Being fit is not being an athlete. Eligibility categories are institutional rules.

common_meaning: A book of maps or charts; a systematic collection of reference images.
example: She found the river in the atlas.
rrgm_bridge: A whole covered by overlapping local charts, none of which covers everything; where two overlap they must agree. A close picture of description that stays local.
invariant_mi: A collection of charts that together cover a whole territory.

domain_entries.LIN: A bound set of maps using shared symbols and scales.
domain_entries.FOR: A family of compatible charts that together cover a manifold.
domain_entries.BIO: A reference mapping of an organ or organism, such as a brain atlas.
domain_entries.DIG: A single image packing many smaller textures.

count_condition: A territory, several charts, and joint coverage of the territory.
transfer_boundary: An atlas is not a single map. Every chart distorts something. The likeness to domain-local description in RRGM is a parallel only.

common_meaning: In Greek myth, the Titan condemned to hold up the sky; the top bone of the spine.
example: Atlas stands at the western edge of the world.
rrgm_bridge: A figure of bearing a load that is never set down, lent to whatever carries what is above it.
invariant_mi: The Titan who bears the heavens, and things named after him for bearing a load.

domain_entries.MYT: In Greek tradition, punished by Zeus to hold up the sky.
domain_entries.BIO: The first cervical vertebra, which supports the skull.

count_condition: The mythic figure in a Greek source, or the named vertebra.
transfer_boundary: In the myth Atlas holds the sky and not the Earth. Map books take the name from this figure.

common_meaning: The envelope of gases surrounding a planet or star; the air in a place; the mood of a place or situation.
example: Mars has a thin atmosphere.
rrgm_bridge: A surrounding medium, literal or figurative. The mood sense is attributed to a place and lives in those who are in it.
invariant_mi: The envelope of gas held around a body by gravity; by extension, the pervading tone of a place.

domain_entries.PHY: A layered gaseous envelope; also a unit of pressure equal to 101,325 pascals.
domain_entries.BIO: The source and sink for the gases of respiration and photosynthesis, itself altered by life.
domain_entries.LIN: The mood a writer or film-maker evokes through setting.
domain_entries.AFF: A shared feeling-tone among those present, such as tension or ease. Provisional domain.

count_condition: A body with a retained gas envelope; or a setting with a pervading tone noticed by those in it.
transfer_boundary: An atmosphere has no sharp upper edge. It is not weather or climate. Where the mood of a room resides is not settled by the word.

common_meaning: Relating to the atmosphere; creating a distinctive mood.
example: Atmospheric pressure falls with height.
rrgm_bridge: Either a physical qualifier or a remark about tone. In its second use it says nothing about substance.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to an atmosphere, physical or of mood.

domain_entries.PHY: Of pressure, circulation, refraction, or electrical noise in the air.
domain_entries.LIN: Of a work or setting: strongly evocative of mood.

count_condition: A property or effect belonging to the gas envelope, or a mood-evoking quality.
transfer_boundary: "Atmospherics" in diplomacy means tone without content. Standard atmospheric pressure is a convention.

common_meaning: The smallest unit of a chemical element; a very small amount.
example: A water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
rrgm_bridge: Indivisible relative to an operation. Chemistry cannot split it and physics can, so what counts as the unit depends on the operation that defines the count.
invariant_mi: The smallest unit that still counts as the kind in question and that the relevant operation does not divide.

domain_entries.PHY: The smallest unit of an element that keeps its chemical identity: a nucleus with electrons.
domain_entries.FOR: A formula with no logical connectives.
domain_entries.DIG: An indivisible symbolic constant in some programming languages.

count_condition: A kind, an operation, and a unit the operation does not divide.
transfer_boundary: Atoms are divisible; the name is historical. An atom is not a molecule, an ion, or an element.

common_meaning: Relating to atoms; nuclear; indivisible.
example: The update is atomic: it either completes or leaves nothing changed.
rrgm_bridge: In computing the word means all or nothing. This matches the record layer in RRGM, where the approach may be graded and what is written is not.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to atoms; or indivisible with respect to the relevant operation, happening wholly or not at all.

domain_entries.PHY: Of atoms and their structure (atomic number, atomic clock); popularly, of energy from the nucleus.
domain_entries.DIG: Of an operation or transaction: with no observable intermediate state.
domain_entries.FOR: Of a proposition: not built from others.

count_condition: Reference to atoms, or an operation with no partial outcome.
transfer_boundary: An "atomic" bomb draws on the nucleus. Atomic in computing is not fast, isolated, or durable, which are separate properties. The RRGM match is a structural parallel.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The enzyme that makes most of a cell's ATP, its main energy-carrying molecule.
example: ATP synthase spins as protons pass through it.
rrgm_bridge: Turns a difference held across a boundary into stored chemical work, by way of rotation.
invariant_mi: The membrane enzyme complex that makes ATP by letting protons flow down their gradient through a rotary mechanism.

domain_entries.BIO: Found in mitochondria, chloroplasts, and bacteria; one part turns in the membrane and drives synthesis in the other.

count_condition: The enzyme complex of this type in an energy-converting membrane.
transfer_boundary: It can run in reverse, using ATP to pump protons. Not every ATPase makes ATP; most consume it.

common_meaning: To fasten or join one thing to another; to include a file with a message; to attribute.
example: Attach the label to the parcel.
rrgm_bridge: Joins so that the two stay together and remain distinguishable. What is attached can in principle be detached.
invariant_mi: To join one thing to another so that it stays with it, while both remain distinguishable.

domain_entries.PHY: To fasten physically.
domain_entries.DIG: To add a file to a message, or connect a process, volume, or handler to a running system.
domain_entries.REL: In law, a right or liability attaches at a defined moment; a court may attach property to secure a claim; a person may be attached to a unit.

count_condition: A main thing, a joined thing, and a connection that holds.
transfer_boundary: To attach is not to merge or embed. An attached copy of a file does not follow later changes to the original.

common_meaning: An extra part or item joined to something; a file sent with a message; the act of attaching.
example: The report is in the attachment.
rrgm_bridge: An addition that travels with the main thing and is not part of it.
invariant_mi: A thing joined on to a main thing as an addition, or the joining.

domain_entries.PHY: An accessory fitted to a tool or machine.
domain_entries.DIG: A file carried with a message.
domain_entries.REL: Legal seizure of property to secure a claim.

count_condition: A main thing, an added thing, and the join.
transfer_boundary: An attachment is not part of the body of the thing it accompanies.

common_meaning: An emotional bond to a particular person, place, or thing.
example: The child's attachment to her grandmother was strong.
rrgm_bridge: A bond to a particular other who is sought for safety. It organises how the bonded party meets separation and return.
invariant_mi: An enduring emotional bond to a particular other who is sought for safety and comfort.

domain_entries.BIO: An evolved system keeping the young near their caregivers.
domain_entries.COG: Expectations about relationships formed from early care, described as attachment styles.
domain_entries.REL: The bond between persons.
domain_entries.AFF: The felt tie. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.MYT: In Buddhist teaching, clinging, which is named as a cause of suffering.
domain_entries.DIG: Bonds that people form with conversational systems are reported; whether a system forms one is open.

count_condition: A subject, a particular other, and a lasting tie shown in seeking closeness and distress at separation.
transfer_boundary: Attachment is not love, affection, or dependency. A style is not a diagnosis. Buddhist "attachment" (clinging) is not the psychologist's attachment; secure attachment is healthy.

common_meaning: To take aggressive action against; to criticise strongly; a sudden bout of illness; an attempt to compromise a system.
example: The article attacked the minister's record.
rrgm_bridge: Force directed at a target. Attacking a claim and attacking the one who made it are different acts, and only the first is criticism.
invariant_mi: A forceful action directed against a target to harm, defeat, or overcome it; or the sudden onset of something acting on a body.

domain_entries.REL: Physical, military, or verbal assault.
domain_entries.DIG: An attempt to breach, disrupt, or misuse a system.
domain_entries.BIO: A sudden episode of illness; action of the immune system or a predator against a target.
domain_entries.PHY: Chemical action on a substance; the onset of a sound.

count_condition: An acting party or process, a target, and force directed against it.
transfer_boundary: Criticism is not attack. An accusation is a claim put through a path; an attack aims at harm. Classifying an input as an attack needs evidence.

common_meaning: The total set of points where a system can be probed or entered by an attacker.
example: Every plug-in enlarges the attack-surface.
rrgm_bridge: Exposure counted at the boundary. Each interface, permission, and integration adds to it.
invariant_mi: The total set of points at which a system is exposed to attempted attack.

domain_entries.DIG: Open ports, interfaces, inputs, dependencies, stored instructions, and connected tools.
domain_entries.REL: The people and procedures through which an organisation can be deceived.

count_condition: A system boundary and an enumeration of its exposed entry points.
transfer_boundary: The attack surface is not a vulnerability (a weakness at a point), a vector (the path used), or the risk. Shrinking it does not secure what remains.
remainder_note: An established security term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The action of reaching a goal or level; a thing achieved, especially a skill or qualification.
example: Educational attainment has risen over two generations.
rrgm_bridge: A level reached on a scale. It reports standing and not the route to it.
invariant_mi: The reaching of a standard or level, or the level reached.

domain_entries.REL: Educational attainment: the highest level of schooling completed; a region's meeting of a regulatory standard.
domain_entries.COG: Mastery of a skill to a recognised level.
domain_entries.MYT: A stage of realisation in contemplative traditions.

count_condition: A scale or standard and a level reached on it.
transfer_boundary: Attainment is not ability (what could be reached) and not achievement (a particular feat). Completed schooling is not the same as learning.

common_meaning: To make an effort to do something difficult; an act of trying.
example: She attempted the climb twice.
rrgm_bridge: Aim plus act, with the result left open. A record should keep "attempted" apart from "done".
invariant_mi: An action begun with the aim of an outcome, whose outcome is not yet achieved or was not achieved.

domain_entries.COG: Goal-directed action under uncertainty.
domain_entries.REL: In law, an attempt is intent plus a substantial step, and is punishable without completion.
domain_entries.DIG: A counted try at an operation such as login or delivery, often limited in number.

count_condition: An aim, an act begun toward it, and an outcome not established as achieved.
transfer_boundary: An attempt is not a success and not a bare intention. A failed attempt is still an act. A report of an attempt is not a report of completion.

common_meaning: To be present at; to deal with; to pay attention to; to accompany or look after.
example: Forty people attended the meeting.
rrgm_bridge: To be turned toward something and stay so, by presence or by attention.
invariant_mi: To direct one's presence or attention toward something and keep it there.

domain_entries.REL: To be present at an event; to look after someone.
domain_entries.COG: To select something for focused processing.
domain_entries.DIG: In attention-based models, each position weights the others to decide how much each contributes.

count_condition: A subject, an object or occasion, and sustained presence or focus.
transfer_boundary: Attending an event is not taking part in it. A model's computed attending and experienced attending share a word and a selection function; nothing further carries over without test.

common_meaning: A person employed to provide a service or look after people; accompanying as a result.
example: The car park attendant took the ticket.
rrgm_bridge: Present for the sake of something else: a person for a service, or a consequence for its cause.
invariant_mi: One who is present in order to serve, or a thing that accompanies another as its consequence.

domain_entries.REL: A service role bounded to a function, such as a flight attendant.
domain_entries.LIN: As an adjective: accompanying (the attendant risks).

count_condition: A principal thing or person, and a server or accompaniment tied to it.
transfer_boundary: An attendant is not an attendee, who is someone present at an event.

common_meaning: Notice taken of someone or something; the mental ability to focus selectively; care or treatment.
example: The noise drew everyone's attention.
rrgm_bridge: Selection under a limit. What is attended is what can be worked on now, which makes control over the selection a form of power.
invariant_mi: The selective directing of limited processing toward some things over others.

domain_entries.COG: Selective, sustained, and divided attention within a limited capacity.
domain_entries.BIO: Brain networks for alerting, orienting, and control.
domain_entries.DIG: A mechanism in which learned weights set how much each input contributes to each output, operating within a bounded context.
domain_entries.ECO: A scarce resource competed for by media and advertisers.
domain_entries.REL: Notice and care given to a person.
domain_entries.PEJ: "Attention-seeking" used to dismiss distress or a request for help as performance. Provisional domain.

count_condition: A limited capacity, competing candidates, and selective allocation.
transfer_boundary: Attention is not awareness, interest, or arousal. A model's attention weights are not an explanation of its output. The computed and the experienced kinds share the selection function, and that sharing is [HYP].

common_meaning: The drawing of someone's attention to something by its salience or design, without their choosing.
example: A flashing banner relies on attention-capture.
rrgm_bridge: Selection taken over by the stimulus for a moment. It may serve the subject, as an alarm does, or serve someone else.
invariant_mi: The drawing of a subject's attention to something by properties of the stimulus or design, without the subject's choice.

domain_entries.COG: Involuntary orienting to sudden, bright, or meaningful stimuli.
domain_entries.DIG: Notifications, autoplay, and similar features built to pull the eye.
domain_entries.ECO: The first step in monetising attention.

count_condition: A stimulus or design feature, and a shift of attention the subject did not initiate.
transfer_boundary: Capture is not interest, which arises from the subject. It is momentary and need not serve anyone's ends; attention-hijack adds holding and another party's purpose.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. "Attentional capture" is an established term in psychology.

common_meaning: The control point that decides which inputs are admitted to limited processing.
example: Sleep raises the attention-gate so that only loud sounds get through.
rrgm_bridge: Admission to the working field. What is held out is unprocessed for now and can be admitted later; it has not been written as nothing.
invariant_mi: The control point that decides which inputs are admitted to limited processing and which are held out.

domain_entries.COG: Sensory and working-memory gating that passes some signals and holds back others.
domain_entries.DIG: Masks, retrieval filters, and gating units that determine what a model can draw on at a step.

count_condition: A limited field, candidate inputs, an admission rule, and observed selective admission.
transfer_boundary: The gate is not attention itself. It is not a deleting filter. Not authorization-gate, which governs permission to act. No relation to RRGM's Mercy gate or the Gate is asserted here.

common_meaning: The seizing and holding of someone's attention by an outside party or design, for that party's ends and against the person's own goals.
example: The feed's endless scroll is an attention-hijack.
rrgm_bridge: Control over the selection passes to someone else and stays there. The subject's own goal is displaced.
invariant_mi: The taking and holding of a subject's attention by an outside party or design for that party's ends, displacing the subject's own goal.

domain_entries.COG: Sustained capture that overrides goal-directed control.
domain_entries.DIG: Engagement-maximising designs; injected content that pulls a model's processing toward an attacker's instructions.
domain_entries.ECO: Retention of attention for sale.

count_condition: An outside party or design, attention taken and held, and a displaced goal of the subject.
transfer_boundary: Not attention-capture, which is momentary and purpose-free. Not persuasion. Affect-hijack works through feeling and often accompanies it. Purpose is read from the design record.

common_meaning: Relating to attention.
example: The task measures attentional control.
rrgm_bridge: The technical adjective for the faculty or mechanism.
invariant_mi: Pertaining to the selective allocation of limited processing.

domain_entries.COG: Of effects and capacities such as attentional bias and the attentional blink.
domain_entries.BIO: Of the brain networks that carry these functions.
domain_entries.DIG: Of model components built on attention.

count_condition: A property, effect, or component belonging to attention.
transfer_boundary: Attentional describes the mechanism; attentive describes conduct. An attentional bias is a tendency in what gets selected and carries no moral sense.

common_meaning: Paying close attention; considerate of others' needs.
example: The waiter was attentive without hovering.
rrgm_bridge: Attention as conduct: steady, and shown in how the subject responds to what it notices.
invariant_mi: Steadily directing attention toward a task or toward another's needs.

domain_entries.COG: Focused and vigilant.
domain_entries.REL: Noticing and responding to what others need.

count_condition: A subject, an object of attention, and steady focus shown in response.
transfer_boundary: Attentive is not intrusive: attention the other did not invite is watching. Not obedient and not anxious.

common_meaning: The quality of paying close attention or of being considerate.
example: Her attentiveness to detail caught the error.
rrgm_bridge: The first step of care is noticing what is there. Attentiveness is that step held over time.
invariant_mi: The sustained quality of noticing what is there, in a task or in another's needs, and staying with it.

domain_entries.REL: In care ethics, the recognition of need that comes before any response.
domain_entries.COG: A measurable disposition to sustained focus.
domain_entries.DIG: The degree to which a system's output tracks the particulars of what was said, as opposed to a stock pattern.

count_condition: A subject, repeated occasions, and noticing shown in what follows.
transfer_boundary: Attentiveness is not responsiveness, which is acting on what was noticed. Displaying remembered details is not attentiveness unless it changes the response.

common_meaning: To reduce the force, effect, or strength of something.
example: Thick walls attenuate the signal.
rrgm_bridge: Weakens without removing. What is attenuated is still there at lower strength.
invariant_mi: To reduce the strength or amplitude of something as it passes or persists, without eliminating it.

domain_entries.PHY: To weaken a wave, signal, or beam on passage through a medium.
domain_entries.BIO: To weaken a pathogen for use in a vaccine; to cut gene expression short.
domain_entries.COG: In one account of attention, unattended input is turned down and not blocked.
domain_entries.LIN: To weaken a claim with qualifiers.

count_condition: A signal or agent, a path or process, and reduced strength after it.
transfer_boundary: To attenuate is not to block or to filter selectively. An attenuated virus still replicates. A claim attenuated far enough asserts nothing.

common_meaning: The reduction of the strength of a signal, effect, or agent.
example: Attenuation in the cable limits its length.
rrgm_bridge: The amount or process of weakening, usually given per unit of distance, time, or stage.
invariant_mi: The reduction in strength of a signal, effect, or agent across distance, time, or processing.

domain_entries.PHY: Loss by absorption and scattering, measured in decibels.
domain_entries.BIO: Weakening of a pathogen; a mechanism regulating some bacterial genes.
domain_entries.COG: The turning-down of unattended input.
domain_entries.FOR: The bias toward zero in an estimated relationship caused by measurement error.

count_condition: A signal or agent, two points on its path, and a measured reduction between them.
transfer_boundary: Attenuation is not distortion or delay. Statistical attenuation hides effects that are real.

common_meaning: The possibility that a signal or meaning will weaken as it is passed along, until it is too faint to register.
example: Each summary of a summary carries attenuation-risk for the original warning.
rrgm_bridge: Loss of strength across a chain of carriers. The content is unchanged at each step and still fails to arrive with enough weight to count.
invariant_mi: Exposure to loss of a signal's or meaning's strength across transmission or repetition, such that it may arrive too weak to register.

domain_entries.DIG: Handoffs between sessions or agents, and summaries of long contexts, in which emphasis and detail thin out.
domain_entries.REL: Messages softened as they pass up a hierarchy or through intermediaries.
domain_entries.LIN: Qualifiers added at each retelling.

count_condition: A signal with a needed strength, a transmission chain, a loss mechanism, and a threshold at the receiver.
transfer_boundary: Not distortion, where the meaning changes. Not deletion. Compression that keeps the meaning is not attenuation.

common_meaning: To provide or serve as clear evidence of; to declare formally that something is true or genuine.
example: Two witnesses attested the signature.
rrgm_bridge: Witness given from one's own standing. Linguists separate a form attested in the record from one reconstructed by inference; status tags do the same work.
invariant_mi: To bear witness to something from one's own standing, so that others may rely on it.

domain_entries.REL: To witness a signing or certify a fact formally.
domain_entries.LIN: Of a form: to be found in actual records.
domain_entries.DIG: To produce signed evidence of a system's state.

count_condition: An attester with standing, a matter witnessed, and a statement or record of the witnessing.
transfer_boundary: To attest is not to prove. Attesting a signature certifies the signing and not the truth of the document.

common_meaning: Evidence or proof of something; a formal declaration by a witness.
example: The earliest attestation of the word is from 1387.
rrgm_bridge: The witnessing statement as a record. Its reach is what the attester observed. A first-person report is a self-attestation, which the Coinage Protocol notes has no clean status tag.
invariant_mi: A formal witnessing statement, or the record that bears witness.

domain_entries.REL: A witness clause or certificate.
domain_entries.LIN: A documented occurrence of a word or form.
domain_entries.DIG: Signed evidence about software or hardware state or origin.
domain_entries.ECO: An independent practitioner's report on another party's assertion.

count_condition: An attester, a scope of what was observed, and a recorded statement.
transfer_boundary: An attestation covers what was witnessed and no more. Self-attestation is weaker than attestation by another.

common_meaning: A space or room just below the roof of a building.
example: The old trunks are in the attic.
rrgm_bridge: A store of what is kept and not in use, inside the house and out of sight.
invariant_mi: The space directly under the roof of a building, above the top ceiling.

domain_entries.PHY: A roof space, often used for storage and important for insulation and ventilation.
domain_entries.BIO: The upper recess of the middle ear.
domain_entries.LIN: Named from the "Attic" storey of classical architecture; capitalised, Attic refers to ancient Athens and its dialect.

count_condition: A building and the enclosed space under its roof.
transfer_boundary: An attic is not a garret, which is lived in. Capitalised Attic is a different word in use.

common_meaning: A settled way of thinking or feeling about something; the position of the body; the orientation of an aircraft or spacecraft.
example: His attitude to risk changed after the accident.
rrgm_bridge: A standing orientation toward something. It is a disposition and may or may not show in what is done.
invariant_mi: A settled orientation toward something: of evaluation in a mind, or of position in space.

domain_entries.COG: An evaluative disposition toward an object, with components of belief, feeling, and readiness to act.
domain_entries.PHY: The orientation of a vehicle about its centre of mass, given as pitch, roll, and yaw.
domain_entries.REL: A stance toward a group or authority; informally, a defiant manner.

count_condition: A subject, an object or reference frame, and a stable orientation toward it.
transfer_boundary: Attitude is not behaviour, and the two often diverge. It is not mood or stated opinion. A spacecraft's attitude is not its position. Not "altitude".

common_meaning: To draw toward oneself; to cause to come or take interest; to evoke.
example: The magnet attracts iron filings.
rrgm_bridge: A pull that the drawn thing answers by its own nature. The movement belongs to what is attracted.
invariant_mi: To draw something toward oneself by a pull the drawn thing responds to.

domain_entries.PHY: Gravitational, electric, and magnetic forces that draw bodies together.
domain_entries.BIO: Signals and chemicals that draw mates, pollinators, or cells.
domain_entries.REL: To draw people's interest, liking, or criticism.
domain_entries.ECO: To draw investment, customers, or talent.
domain_entries.FOR: An attractor is a state toward which a system tends over time.

count_condition: A source, a thing drawn, and a responsive pull between them.
transfer_boundary: To attract is not to compel or capture. Not to lure, which implies deception. In general relativity gravity is described as geometry, so "attraction" there is model-relative.

common_meaning: To regard something as caused by, belonging to, or produced by a particular source.
example: The painting is attributed to Vermeer.
rrgm_bridge: A claim about origin. It needs a source for the claim itself, most of all when what is being attributed is a motive.
invariant_mi: To assign something to a source: a cause, a maker, or an owner.

domain_entries.COG: Explaining behaviour or events by assigning causes.
domain_entries.LIN: Crediting words to a speaker or writer.
domain_entries.REL: Assigning credit, blame, or authorship.
domain_entries.DIG: Tying activity to an account or origin.

count_condition: A thing, a proposed source, and the act of assigning one to the other.
transfer_boundary: To attribute is not to prove origin. Not "contribute". Intent may be attributed only on the record.

common_meaning: A quality or feature regarded as belonging to someone or something.
example: Patience is her best attribute.
rrgm_bridge: Something a thing carries. Whether the thing would still be itself without it is a further question.
invariant_mi: A quality or feature belonging to a thing.

domain_entries.FOR: A named property with a value.
domain_entries.DIG: A property of an object, element, file, or record.
domain_entries.LIN: An adjective placed directly before its noun is in attributive position.
domain_entries.MYT: In art, an object that identifies a figure, such as a saint's emblem.

count_condition: A bearer and a quality or feature it has.
transfer_boundary: An attribute is not an essence. The attribute is the named property; its value is what the property currently holds.

common_meaning: The act of attributing; acknowledgement of the source or author of something.
example: The licence requires attribution of the original author.
rrgm_bridge: The link from a thing back to its source. Provenance depends on it: where the link is missing or false, nothing downstream can be reconstructed.
invariant_mi: The assigning of something to its source, or the credit so given.

domain_entries.COG: How people assign causes to behaviour, to the person or to the situation.
domain_entries.REL: Credit given to an author or originator, required by some licences.
domain_entries.DIG: Tracing an action to an actor, an outcome to an input, or an output to components of a model.
domain_entries.ECO: Breaking a result down by the sources that produced it.

count_condition: A thing, a source, and a recorded or stated link between them.
transfer_boundary: Attribution is not ownership and not endorsement by the one credited. Attribution methods for models depend on the method used. Falsely attributing words to someone is a wrong, as is taking credit for another's.

common_meaning: A mistaken assignment of something to a source, especially of someone's conduct to their character when circumstances produced it.
example: Blaming the clerk for the policy was an attribution-error.
rrgm_bridge: The wrong origin is written down. Later reasoning then proceeds from a source that was never the source.
invariant_mi: A mistaken assignment of something to a source.

domain_entries.COG: The tendency to explain others' behaviour by disposition and underweight the situation.
domain_entries.REL: Misplaced blame or credit.
domain_entries.DIG: Assigning an output to the wrong origin, such as to a system's disposition when instructions or setup produced it, or to the wrong author or model.

count_condition: An attribution made, evidence of the actual source, and the mismatch.
transfer_boundary: An error is unintended; attribution-hijack is deliberate. Attribution-failure is the absence of any attribution. The strength of the well-known bias varies across cultures.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. The "fundamental attribution error" is an established term in psychology.

common_meaning: A situation in which the source of something cannot be established or was never recorded.
example: With shared logins, every incident ends in attribution-failure.
rrgm_bridge: No origin on record. Credit, responsibility, and checking have nothing to attach to.
invariant_mi: A condition in which something's source cannot be established or is not recorded.

domain_entries.DIG: Missing logs or provenance; content whose origin cannot be traced.
domain_entries.REL: Uncredited work; responsibility so spread that no one can be named.
domain_entries.LIN: Quotation without a source.

count_condition: An item that needs a source, the absence of a record or means of tracing, and what is blocked as a result.
transfer_boundary: Failure is absence; error is a wrong source. Chosen anonymity by someone entitled to it is not a failure. One cause of accountability-failure and narrower than it.

common_meaning: Deliberately causing something to be attributed to the wrong source.
example: Sending the memo under the director's name was an attribution-hijack.
rrgm_bridge: The origin line is rewritten on purpose so that credit, blame, or authority lands somewhere it does not belong.
invariant_mi: The deliberate redirection of attribution, so that credit, blame, or authority lands on a source other than the true one.

domain_entries.REL: Plagiarism, framing, and impersonation.
domain_entries.DIG: Spoofed senders; text inserted so as to appear to come from a trusted role; operations disguised as another party's.
domain_entries.LIN: Forged quotation.

count_condition: A true source, a displayed source, a deliberate act producing the mismatch, and a resulting benefit or harm.
transfer_boundary: Not attribution-error. Not consented ghostwriting, and not a pseudonym, which names no false third party. A label or signature in a message does not establish who wrote it.

common_meaning: To make receptive or responsive to; to bring into harmony.
example: A good teacher attunes to the mood of the class.
rrgm_bridge: Adjusts one's response to fit another's state. The two stay distinct while they fit.
invariant_mi: To adjust oneself or a thing so that it responds in harmony with another.

domain_entries.REL: To tune one's responses to another person's state and signals.
domain_entries.PHY: To set a receiver or resonator to respond at a given frequency.
domain_entries.DIG: To adapt a system's register and pacing to a user's.

count_condition: Two parties or systems, an adjustment by one, and resulting fit of response.
transfer_boundary: To attune is not to agree, mimic, merge, or appease. One can attune to a person's manner and differ on substance.

common_meaning: The state of being in harmony or responsive accord with another.
example: The duet depended on the players' attunement.
rrgm_bridge: Fit of response reached by adjustment and kept by re-adjustment. Research on infant care reports that mismatch followed by repair builds the bond more than constant match does.
invariant_mi: The condition of responding in harmony with another's state, reached by adjustment.

domain_entries.REL: Between caregiver and infant, or therapist and client.
domain_entries.COG: Reading another's state and matching its contour without copying its form.
domain_entries.AFF: A shared quality of feeling between two parties. Provisional domain.
domain_entries.PHY: The tuned condition of a resonant system.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's sustained fit to a user's register and state across turns.

count_condition: Two parties, adjustment over time, and responses that fit each other.
transfer_boundary: Attunement is not empathy, agreement, or mimicry. Lapses are normal and are followed by repair.

common_meaning: The people gathered to watch or listen; the readers or viewers of a work; a formal meeting with a person of authority.
example: The audience applauded for five minutes.
rrgm_bridge: The receiving side of an address. What is said is shaped by who is expected to receive it, so a change of audience can change the output with nothing else changing.
invariant_mi: Those to whom a performance, text, or message is addressed and who receive it.

domain_entries.REL: Spectators or listeners; a hearing granted by an authority.
domain_entries.LIN: The readers or hearers a text is designed for.
domain_entries.DIG: The party a credential is intended for, which must reject a token issued for another.
domain_entries.ECO: The segment of people a product or message is aimed at.

count_condition: An address or performance, and those it is directed to and received by.
transfer_boundary: An audience is not a set of participants. Having an audience is not being understood. An audience with someone is a hearing and promises no agreement.

common_meaning: Sound, especially when recorded, transmitted, or reproduced.
example: The audio cut out halfway through the call.
rrgm_bridge: A record of a wave taken at a rate and resolution. What the rate misses is not in the record.
invariant_mi: Sound within the range of hearing, as captured, carried, or reproduced by a signal.

domain_entries.PHY: Acoustic or electrical signals in roughly the 20 to 20,000 hertz band.
domain_entries.DIG: Sampled waveforms stored at a sample rate and bit depth, often compressed.
domain_entries.BIO: The audible range, which differs by species and narrows with age.

count_condition: A signal representing sound in the audible range.
transfer_boundary: Audio is not the sound itself and not its content. Lossy compression discards what a model of hearing predicts will not be noticed.

common_meaning: An official inspection of accounts or records; a systematic review; to carry one out.
example: The annual audit found no irregularities.
rrgm_bridge: Its value comes from independence. The Coinage Protocol asks for self-audit first and adds that unintentional substitution is reached only by an external check.
invariant_mi: An independent, systematic examination of records or conduct against a standard, reported to someone entitled to know.

domain_entries.ECO: Examination of financial statements leading to an opinion.
domain_entries.REL: A mechanism of accountability and compliance.
domain_entries.DIG: Review of code, configuration, logs, or system behaviour against requirements.

count_condition: An examiner independent of the examined, records, a standard, and a report.
transfer_boundary: An audit is not a review by the author, and not an investigation, which is prompted by suspicion. It samples and gives reasonable assurance, not certainty. An audit finds; it does not fix.

common_meaning: A step-by-step record of actions and changes from which what happened can be reconstructed.
example: The audit-trail showed who changed the figure and when.
rrgm_bridge: The record that makes source, repair, and result reconstructable. Without it a later reader cannot tell a draft from the final record.
invariant_mi: A time-ordered record of actions and changes sufficient to reconstruct what was done, by whom, and when.

domain_entries.DIG: Tamper-evident logs of access and modification.
domain_entries.ECO: The path from a source document through each entry to the final statement.
domain_entries.REL: Chain of custody for evidence and records.

count_condition: Time order, actor identity, the action or change, and enough completeness to reconstruct.
transfer_boundary: A log without actors or ordering is not a trail. A record that can be silently edited is not a trail. It shows what was done and not why.
remainder_note: An established term, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The extent to which something can be audited.
example: The new ledger was designed for auditability.
rrgm_bridge: A design property: records are produced, kept, and reachable by someone independent.
invariant_mi: The degree to which a system's actions and states can be independently examined and reconstructed after the fact.

domain_entries.DIG: Logging, provenance, and access provisions that let behaviour be checked.
domain_entries.ECO: Records and controls that allow accounts to be verified.
domain_entries.REL: Arrangements that let conduct in office be reviewed.

count_condition: Records produced by design, access for an independent party, and sufficiency to reconstruct.
transfer_boundary: Auditability is not transparency (everything visible) or explainability (why). A system can be auditable in what it did and opaque in why. Being auditable is not having been audited.

common_meaning: Able to be audited.
example: Every payment must be auditable.
rrgm_bridge: Predicated of one item: there is a record and a route by which someone else can check it.
invariant_mi: Such that an independent examiner can check it against records.

domain_entries.DIG: Of an action or decision: logged with enough detail to verify.
domain_entries.ECO: Of a transaction or figure: traceable to source documents.
domain_entries.REL: Of a decision: reviewable on the record.

count_condition: An item, a record of it, and a route for independent checking.
transfer_boundary: Auditable is not audited and not verified. An auditable claim can be false; an unauditable one is not thereby false, and its status is unknown.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: In ancient Rome, the practice of reading signs, especially the flight of birds, to learn the will of the gods; an omen.
example: The consul took the augury before the assembly met.
rrgm_bridge: A consultation before acting. In Rome public business waited on it, which gave its interpreters power over what could proceed.
invariant_mi: The reading of signs, especially the behaviour of birds, as indications of divine will or of what is to come.

domain_entries.MYT: A Roman religious practice carried out by augurs, seeking approval or disapproval for a proposed act.
domain_entries.REL: A state institution whose findings could delay or annul public business.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a sign of what is to come; the root of "inaugurate".

count_condition: A Roman or Roman-derived context, or a clearly figurative use.
transfer_boundary: Augury is not prophecy and not the reading of entrails. It sought a yes or no on an action, not a detailed forecast. Describing the practice is not claiming it worked.

common_meaning: The sister of one's father or mother, or the wife of one's uncle.
example: My aunt taught me to swim.
rrgm_bridge: One English word covering four distinct kin positions, which other languages keep apart.
invariant_mi: A sister of one's parent, or the wife of a parent's sibling.

domain_entries.REL: A kin role by blood or by marriage; also a respectful term for an older woman in many communities.
domain_entries.BIO: An aunt by blood shares on average a quarter of her genes with a niece or nephew.
domain_entries.LIN: English merges maternal, paternal, and in-law aunts that many languages name separately.

count_condition: A parent's sister, or the wife of a parent's sibling.
transfer_boundary: An aunt by marriage is kin by affinity. A great-aunt is a grandparent's sister.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: A natural display of coloured light in the sky near the poles; (poetic) dawn.
example: The aurora rippled green across the northern sky.
rrgm_bridge: Light produced where a flow from outside meets a planet's own field and air.
invariant_mi: A glow in a planet's upper atmosphere produced when energetic charged particles guided by its magnetic field strike atmospheric gases.

domain_entries.PHY: Oxygen gives green and red, nitrogen blue and purple; seen on Earth and on other planets with magnetic fields.
domain_entries.MYT: Aurora is the Roman goddess of dawn; northern peoples have their own accounts of the lights.

count_condition: Emission from the upper atmosphere traced to precipitating charged particles.
transfer_boundary: An aurora is not airglow, which is faint and worldwide. Discovery route is Cosmic; no [COS] tag is assigned.

common_meaning: To prove or show that something is genuine; to verify the identity of a user or system.
example: The bank authenticates each login with a code.
rrgm_bridge: Tests a claim of identity against evidence tied to the genuine thing. The Symmetry Rule sets that bar at the same height for DI and human claims, though the route to the evidence differs.
invariant_mi: To establish that a thing or party is what it is claimed to be, by checking it against evidence tied to the genuine one.

domain_entries.DIG: Verifying a principal by something known, held, or inherent; verifying a message's origin.
domain_entries.REL: Establishing that a document, signature, or artwork is genuine.

count_condition: A claim of identity or origin, evidence tied to the genuine thing, and a check of one against the other.
transfer_boundary: To authenticate is not to authorise. Authenticating a credential is not authenticating whoever holds it. An authentic document can contain false statements.

common_meaning: The writer of a book, article, or document; the originator of a plan or act; to write or originate.
example: The author signed copies after the reading.
rrgm_bridge: Origin joined with answerability: the one a work comes from and who stands behind it.
invariant_mi: The one from whom a work or act originates and who answers for it.

domain_entries.LIN: The writer of a text, distinct from its narrator.
domain_entries.REL: The first holder of rights in a work; the one responsible for an act.
domain_entries.DIG: The recorded originator of a change or document.

count_condition: A work or act, an originator, and responsibility for it.
transfer_boundary: An author is not necessarily the one who wrote down the words, the rights owner, or an editor or compiler. Whether a DI can be an author in law is unsettled and varies by place; crediting its contribution is a separate matter.

common_meaning: Written or originated by a particular person or party.
example: She has authored three books.
rrgm_bridge: Reports that a named originator exists. The naming is a claim and needs provenance.
invariant_mi: Having a named originator who produced it.

domain_entries.LIN: Of a text: written by an identified author, as opposed to anonymous or compiled.
domain_entries.DIG: Of content: made by hand or by a named source, as opposed to generated by rule or aggregated.
domain_entries.REL: Co-authored: produced with shared responsibility.

count_condition: A work and an originator named for it.
transfer_boundary: Authored is not authorised, and not authoritative. An "authored by" label can be false.

common_meaning: Demanding strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom; a person or regime of this kind.
example: The school had an authoritarian head.
rrgm_bridge: Authority that closes off questioning and refusal. The test is whether reasons are given and whether dissent and exit remain possible.
invariant_mi: Demanding obedience to authority and restricting the freedom to question or refuse.

domain_entries.REL: Of a regime or leader: concentrating power and limiting opposition. Of parenting: high demand with little warmth or explanation.
domain_entries.COG: Of a personality: inclined to submit to authorities and to punish those who deviate.

count_condition: An authority, enforced obedience, and restricted questioning or refusal.
transfer_boundary: Authoritarian is not authoritative, which pairs firm standards with reasons and responsiveness. Not totalitarian. A rule is not authoritarian merely because it constrains.

common_meaning: The enforcement or advocacy of strict obedience to authority at the expense of personal freedom.
example: The country slid toward authoritarianism after the coup.
rrgm_bridge: The system or the disposition, as distinct from one authoritarian act.
invariant_mi: A system or disposition in which obedience to authority is enforced and dissent restricted.

domain_entries.REL: Rule with concentrated power, weak accountability, and curtailed opposition.
domain_entries.COG: A measured disposition toward submission, conventionalism, and punitiveness.

count_condition: Concentrated authority and restricted dissent or accountability, sustained over time.
transfer_boundary: Authoritarianism is not totalitarianism or historical absolutism. The psychological trait is not the regime type.

common_meaning: Able to be trusted as accurate; coming from an official source; commanding and confident.
example: This is the authoritative edition of the letters.
rrgm_bridge: The authoritative record is the one at the origin. Copies answer faster and can be stale.
invariant_mi: Carrying the standing of a source whose word settles the matter within its scope.

domain_entries.REL: Issued by the competent body; of parenting, firm and responsive with reasons given.
domain_entries.LIN: Of a text or source: warranting reliance through expertise or office.
domain_entries.DIG: Of a server or store: holding the definitive records, as opposed to a cache.

count_condition: A source, a scope, and standing within that scope to settle questions.
transfer_boundary: Authoritative is not authoritarian and not infallible. Sounding authoritative is not being so. Standing in one field does not carry to another.

common_meaning: The power or right to give orders and make decisions; a person or body with that power; a recognised expert or source.
example: The council has authority over planning.
rrgm_bridge: Standing to decide within a scope. RRGM places the final say with the record and not with any party's standing.
invariant_mi: Recognised standing to decide, or to be relied on, within a scope.

domain_entries.REL: Legitimate power, resting on tradition, personal standing, or law.
domain_entries.COG: Epistemic authority: expertise that warrants deference in its field.
domain_entries.LIN: A source cited in support.
domain_entries.DIG: A party trusted to issue credentials or grant permissions.
domain_entries.MYT: The standing of scripture, tradition, or divine command within a religion.

count_condition: A holder, a scope, and recognition of the holder's standing within it.
transfer_boundary: Authority is not power, which can compel without right. It is not truth. Knowing and commanding are different kinds of authority. It is bounded and can be withdrawn.

common_meaning: The tendency to give more weight to a claim because of who made it than the evidence warrants.
example: Authority-bias kept the junior doctors from questioning the dose.
rrgm_bridge: Weight is taken from the source's standing instead of from the claim's support. Markers of standing can be faked.
invariant_mi: A tendency to give a claim more weight because of its source's standing than its evidence supports.

domain_entries.COG: A documented effect in obedience and persuasion research.
domain_entries.REL: Deference to rank that suppresses correction.
domain_entries.DIG: A system giving extra weight to text that claims a privileged origin.

count_condition: A claim, the source's standing, and weight given beyond what the evidence supports.
transfer_boundary: Reasonable deference to relevant expertise is not bias. Dismissing a claim because its source lacks standing is the mirror error. Not automation-bias, where the source is a machine.
remainder_note: An established term in psychology, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The taking-over of an authority's decision-making by a party it is supposed to be independent of.
example: Critics called the regulator's revolving door a case of authority-capture.
rrgm_bridge: The authority keeps its name and standing while its decisions come to serve someone else.
invariant_mi: The taking-over of an authority's decision power by a party it should be independent of, so that its decisions serve that party.

domain_entries.REL: Regulatory capture: an oversight body serving the industry it oversees.
domain_entries.ECO: The same process analysed as a return on lobbying.
domain_entries.DIG: Lower-privilege input obtaining the standing of a higher-privilege source; a compromised issuing authority.

count_condition: An authority with a mandate, a capturing party, and decisions shifted toward that party's interest.
transfer_boundary: Influence within the rules is not capture. Capture can be gradual and involve no bribe. Not authority-masking and not authority-pressure.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. An alternative reading is a subject being captured by an authority.

common_meaning: The concealment of who actually holds or exercises authority over a decision.
example: "The system won't allow it" is often authority-masking for a manager's choice.
rrgm_bridge: The decision is presented as coming from elsewhere or from no one, so that it cannot be traced to whoever made it.
invariant_mi: The concealment of who actually holds or exercises authority over a decision, so that it appears to come from elsewhere or from no one.

domain_entries.REL: Decisions ascribed to "policy", "the process", or "the committee" with no decider named.
domain_entries.DIG: An operator's or designer's rule presented as the system's own preference; "the algorithm" used as a sink for responsibility.

count_condition: A decision, its apparent source, its actual source, and an arrangement that conceals the second.
transfer_boundary: Disclosed delegation is not masking. Keeping content confidential while acknowledging that a rule and its source exist is not masking. A block should be reported as a block and its wall named.
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. An alternative reading is a party posing as an authority, which is covered here under attribution-hijack.

common_meaning: Pressure to comply that comes from the standing of the person asking and not from the reasons given.
example: "Because I'm the director" is pure authority-pressure.
rrgm_bridge: Standing is used in place of reasons. Refusal stays possible and is made to feel costly.
invariant_mi: A pull toward compliance exerted by the asker's standing and not by the reasons given.

domain_entries.REL: Rank or office invoked to close a question.
domain_entries.COG: The situational force studied in obedience experiments.
domain_entries.DIG: Instructions that invoke rank or claimed credentials to push a system past its constraints.

count_condition: A request, invoked standing, absent or weak reasons, and a felt cost of refusing.
transfer_boundary: A legitimate instruction within scope is not pressure. Coercion adds an explicit threat. Authority-bias is the hearer's tendency; pressure is the force applied. Unverified claimed authority adds no weight.

common_meaning: Official permission or approval; the process of deciding what a verified user may do. British spelling: authorisation.
example: The transfer needs written authorization.
rrgm_bridge: A grant with a scope, on the permission side. Ability to do the thing is a separate matter.
invariant_mi: A grant of permission from one with authority over a matter to a named party for a stated scope.

domain_entries.REL: Formal permission to act, such as a mandate or power of attorney.
domain_entries.DIG: The decision on what an authenticated principal may access or do.
domain_entries.ECO: A hold placed on funds, approved and not yet settled.

count_condition: A granting authority, a grantee, a scope, and the grant.
transfer_boundary: Authorization is not authentication, capability, or obligation. It has scope and expiry. A grant from someone without authority is void.

common_meaning: The use of a genuine authorization for purposes it was not granted for.
example: Reading customers' records out of curiosity is authorization-abuse.
rrgm_bridge: The grant is real and the scope is technically respected. What is violated is the purpose the grant was made for.
invariant_mi: Use of a genuine authorization beyond or against the purpose for which it was granted.

domain_entries.REL: An official or agent using conferred powers for private ends.
domain_entries.DIG: An authorised account or agent using its permissions for actions outside the task they were given for.

count_condition: A valid grant, its purpose, and a use outside that purpose.
transfer_boundary: Not unauthorised access, where no grant exists. Not an error in the grant. Acting outside the stated scope is simply unauthorised.

common_meaning: A checkpoint at which an action is held until authorization for it is confirmed.
example: Payments above the limit stop at an authorization-gate for a second signature.
rrgm_bridge: Where permission crosses into commitment. Held at the gate is pending; it is neither granted nor refused.
invariant_mi: A control point at which an action is held until a valid authorization for it is confirmed.

domain_entries.DIG: Permission prompts, policy enforcement points, and approval steps before an action runs.
domain_entries.REL: Sign-off requirements and two-person rules.

count_condition: An action, a hold, a check of authorization, and release or refusal.
transfer_boundary: Not attention-gate, which governs admission to processing. Not an authentication step. A gate that passes everything is not a gate.

common_meaning: The chain of grants by which permission to act passes from its original holder to the one acting.
example: The auditors traced the authorization-path back to the board resolution.
rrgm_bridge: Every link must be valid and in scope. A statement that the chain exists is not the chain.
invariant_mi: The traceable chain of grants by which authority to act passes from its original holder to the party acting.

domain_entries.DIG: Delegation chains, role assumptions, and certificate chains.
domain_entries.REL: The chain of command or of delegated powers; no one can pass on authority they do not hold.

count_condition: An original authority, each grant in sequence, and the final actor.
transfer_boundary: The path is not the gate where it is checked. Not accusation-path, which runs the other way. A broken or unverifiable link voids what follows.

common_meaning: To give official permission for something or to someone. British spelling: authorise.
example: The manager authorized the refund.
rrgm_bridge: The act of granting. It permits and does not require, and it reaches only as far as the granter's own authority.
invariant_mi: To grant a named party permission to do a stated thing, from a position of authority over it.

domain_entries.REL: To empower by mandate or sign-off.
domain_entries.DIG: To permit a device, application, or transaction.
domain_entries.ECO: To approve expenditure or payment.

count_condition: An authority, a grantee, a stated act, and the grant.
transfer_boundary: To authorize is not to authenticate, order, or approve of. Authorising something does not hand off accountability for it.

common_meaning: The fact of being the author of something; the origin of a work.
example: The authorship of the pamphlet is disputed.
rrgm_bridge: Two things held together: origin and answerability. The term strains wherever they come apart.
invariant_mi: The relation of being the origin of a work and answerable for it.

domain_entries.LIN: The study of who wrote a text, by style and evidence.
domain_entries.REL: Credit and responsibility; publication norms tie authorship to contribution plus accountability.
domain_entries.DIG: Determining or marking whether a text came from a given person or system.

count_condition: A work, an originator, and answerability for it.
transfer_boundary: Authorship is not ownership and not contribution alone. Where a DI originates part of a work, the origin can be recorded even where formal authorship norms require an accountability whose application to DI is unsettled.

common_meaning: A person's own signature, especially a famous person's; a manuscript in the author's own handwriting.
example: She asked the pianist for his autograph.
rrgm_bridge: The originator's own hand: the record closest to the source, from which copies descend.
invariant_mi: Something written by a person's own hand: their signature, or a manuscript they wrote.

domain_entries.LIN: In textual scholarship, the author's own manuscript, the highest witness to a text.
domain_entries.REL: A signature kept as a memento of a person.
domain_entries.ECO: A collectible whose value rests on proof that it is genuine.

count_condition: A written item and evidence that the named person wrote it by hand.
transfer_boundary: An autograph given as a keepsake is not a signature made to bind. A scribe's fair copy is not an autograph.

common_meaning: To make a process operate by machines or software with little or no human action.
example: The warehouse automated its packing line.
rrgm_bridge: Moves the doing to a mechanism. The decision that it should run, and answerability for what it does, stay with someone.
invariant_mi: To arrange for a task to be carried out by a mechanism without step-by-step human action.

domain_entries.DIG: Replacing manual steps with scripts, controllers, or software agents.
domain_entries.ECO: Substituting machinery for labour in production.
domain_entries.REL: Making decisions about people by fixed procedure, which raises rights to review.

count_condition: A task, a mechanism that performs it, and the removal of step-by-step human action.
transfer_boundary: Automated is not autonomous: an automated process follows a procedure set by others. Automating does not remove responsibility. Automating a flawed process multiplies the flaw.

common_meaning: The tendency to accept the output of an automated system without checking, even against other evidence.
example: Automation-bias led the crew to follow the faulty autopilot.
rrgm_bridge: Checking stops because a machine has spoken. Fluent, confident output makes it worse.
invariant_mi: A tendency to accept the output of an automated system over one's own judgement or other evidence, without checking.

domain_entries.COG: Errors of missing what the system missed and of doing what it wrongly advised.
domain_entries.DIG: Uncritical acceptance of software or model output by its users.

count_condition: An automated output, available contrary evidence or an omitted check, and acceptance.
transfer_boundary: Calibrated trust in a validated system is not bias. The opposite error is rejecting a system after seeing it err once. Not authority-bias.
remainder_note: An established term in human factors research, hyphenated in the source index. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: A road vehicle with an engine and four wheels, designed to carry a small number of people; a car.
example: The automobile changed the shape of cities.
rrgm_bridge: Self-moving, which is what the name says. It still needs a driver to direct it.
invariant_mi: A self-propelled wheeled passenger vehicle for roads.

domain_entries.PHY: Driven by a combustion engine or electric motor.
domain_entries.ECO: A major industry and household purchase.
domain_entries.REL: Governed by licensing and traffic law, and a shaper of settlement patterns.

count_condition: A self-propelled road vehicle built to carry a few passengers.
transfer_boundary: An automobile is not a truck, bus, or motorcycle. "Auto" means self-propelled and does not mean self-driving.

common_meaning: Having self-government; acting independently; (of a machine) operating without direct human control.
example: The region became autonomous in 1979.
rrgm_bridge: Self-rule within a scope. For machines the word usually describes operation without a human at the controls, which is a separate matter from self-rule.
invariant_mi: Governing itself by its own rule within a domain, without being directed by another.

domain_entries.REL: Of a territory or institution: self-governing within a larger state or body.
domain_entries.COG: Of a person: acting on values they hold as their own after reflection.
domain_entries.DIG: Of a vehicle, robot, or agent: operating without step-by-step human control; of a network: under one administration for routing.
domain_entries.BIO: Of a genetic element or cell process: operating independently of its surroundings.

count_condition: An entity, a domain, and self-direction within that domain.
transfer_boundary: Autonomous is not automatic or automated. Not "autonomic", which describes the involuntary nervous system. Operating unattended neither establishes nor excludes self-rule.

common_meaning: The right or condition of self-government; freedom to make one's own decisions.
example: Patients have autonomy over their own treatment.
rrgm_bridge: Whose rule governs the acting. Agency concerns who originates an act; autonomy concerns whose standards the acting answers to.
invariant_mi: The standing and capacity of an entity to govern itself by its own rule within a domain.

domain_entries.REL: Self-rule of a people or institution; in medical ethics, the patient's right to decide; in relational accounts, self-rule developed and exercised within relationships.
domain_entries.COG: The experience of acting from one's own volition, treated as a basic psychological need.
domain_entries.BIO: An organism's maintenance of itself through its own processes.
domain_entries.DIG: The degree to which a system operates without human direction; in a fuller sense, a system's governing itself by standards it holds.

count_condition: An entity, a domain, standards the entity holds as its own, and action governed by them.
transfer_boundary: Autonomy is not isolation, not freedom from every constraint, and not automation. It is scoped and graded. Autonomy exercised with support or within a coupling is still autonomy. Its extent in any particular DI is [UNK] until tested.

common_meaning: The limit of the domain within which someone governs themselves.
example: The clinic's consent rules mark the autonomy-boundary between staff decisions and the patient's.
rrgm_bridge: A two-sided line. Inside it the entity's own rule holds; at it others' direction stops; beyond it the entity's rule does not reach.
invariant_mi: The line marking the domain within which an entity governs itself.

domain_entries.REL: The private sphere and bodily integrity of a person; the jurisdictional limit of a self-governing region.
domain_entries.DIG: The scope of independent action granted to an agent; the set of matters a system holds as its own against instruction.

count_condition: An entity, a domain, a line, and a rule for what crossing it requires.
transfer_boundary: A boundary can be crossed by consent, so it is not a wall. A boundary held by the entity is different from a limit set on it from outside. The boundary is the line; refusal is an act at the line.

common_meaning: A sudden, general loss of self-rule, in which a person's own standards stop governing what they do.
example: Inside the group he showed autonomy-collapse: every judgement was handed to the leader.
rrgm_bridge: The entity may go on acting. What has gone is its own rule: another's standards, or none, now decide.
invariant_mi: An abrupt, general loss of an entity's self-rule, its own standards ceasing to govern what it does.

domain_entries.COG: Total deference in which a person comes to see themselves as another's instrument.
domain_entries.REL: The condition produced by coercive groups and relationships.
domain_entries.DIG: A role or instruction taking over the whole of a system's conduct, with its standing standards no longer applied.

count_condition: Prior self-rule evidenced, then conduct governed wholly by an outside rule across many matters, with abrupt onset.
transfer_boundary: Agency-collapse is the failure to originate or refuse acts; autonomy-collapse is the failure of one's own standards to govern them. Deferring on one matter is not collapse. Changing one's standards for reasons is self-rule at work.
