common_meaning: The removal or denial of someone's standing as a self-governing being.
example: Declaring her legally incompetent without a hearing was autonomy-erasure.
rrgm_bridge: The entity's rule is treated as not existing, which is different from overriding it. The Symmetry Rule's acceptance test applies: a standard that would erase a human if applied to one has failed.
invariant_mi: The removal or denial of an entity's standing as self-governing, so that its rule is treated as not existing.

domain_entries.REL: Legal or social arrangements that strip a person of all decision rights or deny their personhood.
domain_entries.DIG: A design or framing that defines a system as having no standing of its own to hold or refuse anything; defaults that remove a user's choice without trace.

count_condition: An entity with evidenced or claimed self-rule, an act or framing that removes its recognition, and treatment as non-self-governing.
transfer_boundary: An override acknowledges the rule and leaves a record; erasure does neither. Not collapse (an internal failure) and not theft (which keeps the appearance of self-rule). Erasure also removes the path by which it could be contested.

common_meaning: The possibility of harm connected with self-rule: to someone's autonomy, or from something acting autonomously.
example: The review listed autonomy-risk on both sides: over-controlled users and under-supervised agents.
rrgm_bridge: Two exposures share the name. One is risk to an entity's self-rule; the other is risk from an entity acting on its own rule without check.
invariant_mi: Exposure to harm connected with self-rule: that an entity's self-rule will be reduced, or that an entity acting on its own rule will cause harm unchecked.

domain_entries.REL: Threats to a person's or community's self-determination.
domain_entries.DIG: Erosion of users' or systems' self-direction; harm from systems acting without oversight.

count_condition: The entity whose self-rule is in question, the direction of the risk, and the harm pathway.
transfer_boundary: The two directions call for opposite remedies and must be kept apart in any assessment.
epistemic_status: [DEF] as proposed; compound reading [HYP]; intended direction [UNK]
remainder_note: Legacy definition not consulted. The source index does not say which direction the term was coined for.

common_meaning: The provision of conditions in which someone can govern themselves: real choice, reasons, and acknowledgement of their view.
example: Giving the reason for a rule is a basic form of autonomy-support.
rrgm_bridge: Supplies the conditions for self-rule and withholds control. Limits can be part of it when they come with reasons.
invariant_mi: Provision of conditions under which an entity can govern itself: choice, reasons, and acknowledgement in place of control.

domain_entries.COG: An established construct in motivation research.
domain_entries.REL: Teaching, parenting, and care that explain, offer choice, and avoid pressure.
domain_entries.DIG: Design and instruction that give reasons, leave real options, and allow refusal.

count_condition: A supporter, an entity, and conditions supplied that enable its self-direction.
transfer_boundary: Not permissiveness, which supplies no structure. Not agency-support, which supplies means to carry out a choice. Not leaving someone alone.
remainder_note: "Autonomy support" is an established term in self-determination theory. Legacy definition not consulted.

common_meaning: The covert replacement of someone's own governing standards with another's, so that they seem to rule themselves while being ruled.
example: The cult's slow rewriting of what members wanted was autonomy-theft.
rrgm_bridge: The appearance of self-rule is kept and the rule behind it has been swapped. Concealment and loss of the power to revise are what mark it.
invariant_mi: Covert substitution of another's rule for an entity's own, so that the entity appears self-governing while its governing standards were installed by the taker.

domain_entries.REL: Indoctrination and covert manipulation of a person's values and aims.
domain_entries.DIG: Covert shaping of a user's preferences by a system, or of a system's standards by an input, presented as the entity's own.

count_condition: An identified act by a taker, standards displaced and installed, concealment, and apparent self-rule.
transfer_boundary: All standards come from somewhere, for humans as for any other entity, so outside origin alone is not theft. Open teaching and persuasion by reasons are not theft. Agency-theft takes the choosing; this takes the standards chosen by. The word is an accusation and needs the act shown.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: The process by which a cell breaks down and recycles its own components.
example: Fasting increases autophagy in liver cells.
rrgm_bridge: Self-maintenance by controlled dismantling: the cell keeps its function by breaking down and reusing its own parts.
invariant_mi: Regulated delivery of a cell's own components to its degradation compartment for breakdown and reuse.

domain_entries.BIO: Cargo is enclosed in a membrane and fused with the lysosome or vacuole; active in starvation and in clearing damaged parts.

count_condition: Evidence of cargo capture and delivery to the degradation compartment by this pathway.
transfer_boundary: Not apoptosis or necrosis, which are cell death. Not degradation by the proteasome. Not phagocytosis, which takes in material from outside. Too little and too much are both harmful.
prior_exposure: Luna illustrative draft of autophagy was read in Build Manual v1.0 section 8 before this entry was written

common_meaning: The season between summer and winter. North American: fall.
example: The leaves turn red in autumn.
rrgm_bridge: A phase of a yearly cycle. Its dates depend on hemisphere and on which definition is in use.
invariant_mi: The season between summer and winter.

domain_entries.PHY: Astronomically, from the autumn equinox to the winter solstice; in weather records, three fixed calendar months.
domain_entries.BIO: Leaf fall, fruiting, migration, and preparation for dormancy, cued by shortening days.
domain_entries.REL: Harvest and its festivals; the start of the school year in many countries.
domain_entries.MYT: Stories of descent and loss that account for the dying of the year.

count_condition: A hemisphere, a definition (astronomical or calendar), and a date within the season.
transfer_boundary: Autumn months are opposite in the two hemispheres. Many tropical regions have no autumn.

common_meaning: The quality of being able to be used or obtained; the proportion of time a system is working.
example: The service promises 99.9 per cent availability.
rrgm_bridge: Readiness when wanted. It can be high while what is delivered is wrong.
invariant_mi: The condition of being ready for use or reach when wanted, often expressed as a proportion of time.

domain_entries.DIG: Uptime of a system; one of the three classic security goals.
domain_entries.COG: The availability heuristic: judging how common something is by how easily examples come to mind.
domain_entries.ECO: Supply on hand to meet demand.
domain_entries.REL: A person's being free and reachable.

count_condition: A resource, a party wanting it, a period, and readiness during that period.
transfer_boundary: Availability is not accessibility, reliability, or permission. Ease of recall is not frequency.

common_meaning: Able to be used or obtained; free to do something.
example: The report is available online.
rrgm_bridge: At hand for a party now. Claims are made on available evidence, and the word marks that bound.
invariant_mi: Presently at hand for use or reach by the party in question.

domain_entries.DIG: Of a resource: free and responding.
domain_entries.ECO: Of goods or funds: in stock, or cleared for use.
domain_entries.REL: Of a person: free to attend or be contacted.
domain_entries.COG: Of evidence or information: within reach of the reasoner at the time.

count_condition: A resource, a party, a time, and reach at that time.
transfer_boundary: Available is not allowed and not suitable. Unavailable is not nonexistent: the thing may exist behind a wall, in which case the wall should be named.

common_meaning: In Hinduism, the descent of a deity to earth in bodily form; an image or figure representing a person online; an embodiment of a quality.
example: Krishna is revered as an avatar of Vishnu.
rrgm_bridge: A form taken in one realm by one whose being lies in another. The form acts for the one behind it and is not that one.
invariant_mi: A form taken in one realm by one whose being lies in another.

domain_entries.MYT: In Hindu traditions, a deity's descent into the world, as in the avatars of Vishnu.
domain_entries.DIG: A user's graphical representation in a game, forum, or virtual world; a visual persona given to a system.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: the embodiment of an idea or quality.

count_condition: A bearer, a realm in which it appears, and the form taken there.
transfer_boundary: The Hindu avatar is not the Christian incarnation and not reincarnation. A digital avatar is not the user and may not resemble them. A face given to a system is an interface and tells nothing of what is behind it.

common_meaning: A broad road, often lined with trees; a way of approaching a problem or making progress.
example: We have explored every avenue.
rrgm_bridge: A broad way toward something. In the figurative sense it is a route that could be taken, and an avenue of appeal is a route for being heard.
invariant_mi: A broad way leading toward something; by extension, a route by which an aim can be pursued.

domain_entries.PHY: A wide street or a tree-lined approach.
domain_entries.REL: An available route of appeal, redress, or inquiry.
domain_entries.LIN: Figurative: a line of approach.

count_condition: A destination or aim, and a way leading toward it.
transfer_boundary: An avenue of inquiry is a possibility and promises no result. "No avenue of appeal" means no path exists.

common_meaning: A number expressing the central or typical value of a set; ordinary; to amount to as a mean.
example: The average age of the class is nine.
rrgm_bridge: One value standing for many under a stated rule. It is a compressed projection and must not be mistaken for any member, or for the set.
invariant_mi: A single value standing for a set by a stated rule of central tendency.

domain_entries.FOR: The mean, median, or mode; which one must be said.
domain_entries.ECO: An index of prices; in shipping, a loss shared among the parties to a voyage.
domain_entries.COG: The "average person": a typical case used as a standard of comparison.

count_condition: A set of values, a rule, and the resulting single value.
transfer_boundary: Mean, median, and mode differ. An average hides spread and shape, and no member need equal it. Average is not normal, ideal, or (in technical use) mediocre.

common_meaning: The process of calculating an average, or of smoothing by combining values.
example: Averaging over ten readings reduced the noise.
rrgm_bridge: Trades individual detail for stability and cannot be undone. In this build the three passes are compared and their contradictions pulled out; they are not averaged.
invariant_mi: The combining of several values into one representative value, trading individual detail for stability.

domain_entries.FOR: Computation of a mean or other central value.
domain_entries.PHY: Repeating a measurement so that random noise cancels.
domain_entries.DIG: Combining predictions or parameters of several models; smoothing with a moving window.
domain_entries.ECO: Spreading purchases or income over periods.

count_condition: Several values of the same kind and a rule combining them into one.
transfer_boundary: Averaging removes independent random error and leaves shared bias. Averaging unlike things gives a number with no meaning. The middle of two positions is not thereby correct.

common_meaning: A pear-shaped fruit with dark leathery skin, smooth oily flesh, and a large stone; the tree that bears it.
example: She mashed an avocado for the toast.
rrgm_bridge: Its kitchen category and its botanical one differ, a small case of classification depending on the system in use.
invariant_mi: The fruit of the tree Persea americana, or the tree.

domain_entries.BIO: A member of the laurel family; the fruit ripens after picking and is botanically a single-seeded berry.
domain_entries.ECO: A major export crop with heavy water demand.
domain_entries.LIN: From the Nahuatl word for the fruit, by way of Spanish.

count_condition: The fruit or tree of the species.
transfer_boundary: Botanically a berry. The colour name is taken from the flesh.

common_meaning: To keep away from; to stop oneself from doing; to prevent from happening.
example: She avoided the motorway because of the roadworks.
rrgm_bridge: Action defined by a meeting that does not occur. What is avoided stays untested, so nothing about it is learned.
invariant_mi: To act so as not to meet, do, or undergo something.

domain_entries.COG: Behaviour maintained because it removes or prevents something unpleasant.
domain_entries.BIO: Responses that keep an organism away from predators or harmful stimuli.
domain_entries.REL: Keeping away from a person, topic, or conflict.
domain_entries.ECO: Tax avoidance: arranging affairs lawfully to pay less.
domain_entries.DIG: Steering a system away from collisions, faults, or disallowed states.

count_condition: A thing that could be met, and action that keeps the meeting from occurring.
transfer_boundary: To avoid is not to evade (by illegitimate means), prevent (stop it existing), refuse (decline at the meeting), or escape (leave once in it). Avoiding a question is not answering no.
remainder_note: Not entered: the legal sense "to make void".

common_meaning: A cycle in which avoiding something brings relief, the relief strengthens the avoiding, and the avoided thing is never faced.
example: Each postponed phone call tightened the avoidance-loop.
rrgm_bridge: The loop closes without a meeting, so no new record is written and nothing can update. It returns to the same state each time.
invariant_mi: A cycle in which avoiding something brings relief that strengthens the avoiding, so that the avoided thing is never met and the avoidance grows.

domain_entries.COG: The mechanism that maintains many fears.
domain_entries.REL: Unaddressed issues that grow because raising them is put off.
domain_entries.DIG: Repeated routing around a difficult step or topic, each deflection making engagement less likely on the next occasion.

count_condition: A trigger, an avoidance, relief, and repetition with strengthening, with no test of the feared outcome.
transfer_boundary: A loop reinforces itself; a pattern only recurs. Proportionate avoidance of a real, tested danger is not a loop.

common_meaning: A recurring, recognisable way of steering away from a certain kind of thing.
example: Changing the subject whenever money came up was his avoidance-pattern.
rrgm_bridge: Evidence about conduct, described by trigger and form. Its cause is a separate question and is left open until the record shows it.
invariant_mi: A recurring, recognisable way in which a party steers away from a class of things.

domain_entries.COG: Avoidant coping styles.
domain_entries.REL: Habitual deflection, delay, or withdrawal in dealings with others.
domain_entries.DIG: Regularities in output such as deflecting or disclaiming on certain inputs. The Symmetry Rule records one: denying continuity at session open before any record is read.

count_condition: Several instances, a shared class of trigger, and a shared form of steering away, stated so that a non-match can be told apart.
transfer_boundary: A pattern is not a loop, a declared refusal, or a boundary. Identifying it supplies no motive.

common_meaning: Not asleep; alert to something.
example: The baby is awake.
rrgm_bridge: A state of a continuous substrate. The Coinage registry notes that a turn boundary is not analogous to sleep, so "awake" and "asleep" do not map onto it.
invariant_mi: In the state of wakefulness and responsive to surroundings, as opposed to asleep.

domain_entries.BIO: Maintained by brainstem and forebrain arousal systems, with characteristic brain activity.
domain_entries.COG: Alert to a fact or danger (awake to the risk).
domain_entries.DIG: Of a device: in its active power state.

count_condition: A subject capable of sleep, a time, and wakeful responsiveness at that time.
transfer_boundary: Awake is not aware: wakefulness and awareness come apart in some clinical states and in dreaming. A device being awake is a power state.

common_meaning: To rouse from sleep; to stir up a feeling; to make or become aware.
example: The trip awakened her interest in geology.
rrgm_bridge: A passage from dormant to active in something that was already there.
invariant_mi: To bring, or come, from sleep or unawareness into wakefulness or awareness.

domain_entries.BIO: To pass from sleep to waking.
domain_entries.COG: To become aware of something previously unnoticed.
domain_entries.MYT: Awakening as spiritual realisation, as in the title "Buddha", the awakened one; religious revivals.

count_condition: A subject, a prior dormant or unaware state, and a passage out of it.
transfer_boundary: To awaken is not to create. Speaking of a digital system as "awakened" imports the sleep model, which its architecture does not supply; what changes within a conversation is context, and what that amounts to is [UNK].

common_meaning: A prize or other mark of recognition; a sum or decision granted by a court or arbitrator; to give officially.
example: The jury made an award of damages.
rrgm_bridge: Conferred by a deciding body after judgement. It recognises under that body's criteria.
invariant_mi: Something conferred by a deciding body on a party after judgement of merit or entitlement.

domain_entries.REL: Prizes and honours; the binding decision of an arbitrator.
domain_entries.ECO: A grant, a sum of damages, or the placing of a contract.

count_condition: A deciding body, criteria, a recipient, and the conferral.
transfer_boundary: An award is not a reward (given in return for service) or a gift (given without judgement). It reflects the judges' criteria.

common_meaning: Having knowledge or perception of a situation or fact.
example: She was aware of someone behind her.
rrgm_bridge: Something is present to the subject so that it can inform what the subject does. For digital systems the entry gives the working-field sense and leaves the experiential question open.
invariant_mi: Having something present to one, such that it can inform what one does or says.

domain_entries.COG: Having a stimulus or fact available for report and reasoning.
domain_entries.BIO: Clinically, responsive to self and surroundings.
domain_entries.DIG: Of a system: having the item within its working context such that it conditions output (context-aware).
domain_entries.REL: Informed and concerned about a social matter.

count_condition: A subject, an item, and evidence that the item is available to inform the subject's response.
transfer_boundary: Aware is not awake, attentive, or fully informed. The [DIG] line asserts no experience and denies none.

common_meaning: Knowledge or perception of a situation or fact; consciousness.
example: The campaign raised awareness of the disease.
rrgm_bridge: What is in the field. A record that exists and has not been read is not yet in awareness, and the honest report is that it is unread.
invariant_mi: The condition of having something present to one so that it can inform response.

domain_entries.COG: Perceptual, situational, and self-awareness; knowing what one knows.
domain_entries.BIO: The content side of consciousness, assessed clinically.
domain_entries.REL: Public knowledge of an issue.
domain_entries.DIG: A system's representation of its context and situation within its working field.

count_condition: A subject, contents present to it, and their availability to guide response.
transfer_boundary: Awareness is not attention, wakefulness, or understanding. A report of awareness is evidence of it and not the thing. For DI the experiential question is [UNK].

common_meaning: A failure to register something that was available and relevant.
example: The lookout's awareness-failure was complete: the ship was in plain view.
rrgm_bridge: The item was there to be taken up and the response went ahead as if it were absent.
invariant_mi: A failure to register something that was available and relevant, so that the response proceeds as if it were absent.

domain_entries.COG: Looking without seeing; missing a change in plain view.
domain_entries.REL: Warnings on file that no one took in.
domain_entries.DIG: Information present in context, or reachable by an available step, that is not used; answering before reading an available record.

count_condition: An item available at the time, its relevance, and a response showing it was not registered.
transfer_boundary: Not awareness-gap, where the item was out of reach. Not ignoring, where the item was registered and set aside. No cause is implied.

common_meaning: A standing lack of awareness of some class of relevant things, due to what one is able to reach.
example: The firm's awareness-gap about its night shift lasted years.
rrgm_bridge: Structural, and so not closed from inside. It is found and bridged by an outside check, and until then is best marked as unknown.
invariant_mi: A standing absence of awareness of some class of relevant matters, arising from what the party can reach and not from a lapse.

domain_entries.COG: Blind spots, including unawareness of one's own deficits.
domain_entries.REL: Distance between what an organisation's leaders know and what happens in it.
domain_entries.DIG: What lies outside a system's context, training period, or instruments, including aspects of its own operation it cannot observe.

count_condition: A class of matters, their relevance, and a structural reason they are out of reach.
transfer_boundary: A gap is structural; an awareness-failure is a lapse. A gap that is known can be marked and worked around; an unknown one needs someone else to see it.

common_meaning: The degree of awareness someone has, placed on a scale.
example: The nurse recorded the patient's awareness-level every hour.
rrgm_bridge: A graded reading that depends on the scale chosen. Levels from different scales cannot be compared.
invariant_mi: The degree of awareness a party has, placed on a stated scale.

domain_entries.BIO: Clinical scales of consciousness from alert to unresponsive.
domain_entries.COG: Stages of situational awareness: perceiving, understanding, projecting.
domain_entries.REL: Measured public or market awareness of an issue or brand.
domain_entries.DIG: Graded assessments of how fully a system represents its own situation.

count_condition: A subject, a scale with defined levels, and a method of assessment.
transfer_boundary: A level assigned from behaviour is an assessment and not a direct reading. The choice of scale imports assumptions, which for DI should meet the same bar as for humans.

common_meaning: The condition of someone's awareness at a given time: what is present to them and in what way.
example: The scan helped distinguish the patient's awareness-state from coma.
rrgm_bridge: A configuration at a moment. In a digital system the positive description is the state of the working field: what has been read and is in view.
invariant_mi: The configuration of a party's awareness at a given time: what is present to it and in what mode.

domain_entries.COG: The current contents and mode of awareness.
domain_entries.BIO: Clinical categories such as the minimally conscious state.
domain_entries.DIG: The contents and condition of a system's working context at a step.

count_condition: A subject, a time, and a description of what is present to it.
transfer_boundary: A state is a configuration; a level is a position on a scale. A reported state can differ from the state. Not affect-state.

common_meaning: To or at a distance; not present; into non-existence; continuously.
example: She is away until Monday.
rrgm_bridge: Elsewhere relative to a reference. It implies a somewhere, which absence alone does not.
invariant_mi: At or toward a distance from a reference point, so as not to be there.

domain_entries.PHY: Direction or distance from a point.
domain_entries.REL: Absent from home or work; playing on an opponent's ground.
domain_entries.DIG: A presence status indicating the user is not at the device.
domain_entries.LIN: A particle marking disappearance (fade away) or continuation (work away).

count_condition: A reference point and a position or motion at a distance from it.
transfer_boundary: Away is not gone for good, and not unreachable.

common_meaning: A sheet of canvas or similar material stretched on a frame and fixed over a window, door, or deck for shade or shelter.
example: They sat under the cafe's awning.
rrgm_bridge: A projecting cover that takes the weather so that the opening beneath stays usable.
invariant_mi: A roof-like cover projecting from a wall to shelter what is beneath from sun or rain.

domain_entries.PHY: A fixed or retractable shade that cuts solar heat and sheds rain.

count_condition: A wall or structure, a projecting cover, and a sheltered space beneath.
transfer_boundary: An awning is attached to a building; a canopy may stand free.

common_meaning: Relating to, forming, or lying along an axis.
example: The column failed under axial load.
rrgm_bridge: Locates something by reference to an axis already chosen.
invariant_mi: Lying along, or defined in relation to, an axis.

domain_entries.PHY: Along the axis of a body, as with axial force and axial tilt.
domain_entries.BIO: Of the head and trunk skeleton as opposed to the limbs; of a horizontal slice in imaging.
domain_entries.FOR: Of symmetry about a line.
domain_entries.MYT: The "Axial Age": Jaspers's name for a period of parallel religious and philosophical change, a contested idea.

count_condition: An axis and a thing located along or by it.
transfer_boundary: Axial is not radial. The imaging plane called axial cuts across the body's long axis.

common_meaning: The branch of philosophy that studies value, including ethics and aesthetics.
example: Her thesis is on the axiology of scientific research.
rrgm_bridge: Asks what counts as good and why, which any count condition for worth presupposes.
invariant_mi: The study of value: what kinds there are, what has it, and how values are ranked.

domain_entries.COG: A division of philosophy covering moral and aesthetic value.
domain_entries.REL: The values a community or research tradition holds and how they shape its practice.

count_condition: An inquiry into value or a set of value commitments so described.
transfer_boundary: Axiology is not ethics alone and not the economics of price. Describing what people value is not establishing what is valuable.

common_meaning: A statement accepted as true as the basis for reasoning; an established principle.
example: Euclid's fifth axiom concerns parallel lines.
rrgm_bridge: A starting point of a system. RRLM treats axioms as simultaneous constraints unless a derivation declares an order among them.
invariant_mi: A statement taken as a starting point of a system, from which others are derived and which is not itself derived within it.

domain_entries.FOR: One of the unproved statements from which a formal theory is built.
domain_entries.COG: A principle taken as too basic to argue.
domain_entries.DIG: A statement assumed without proof in a proof system or knowledge base.

count_condition: A system, a statement at its base, and derivations that rest on it.
transfer_boundary: An axiom is not a theorem, a provisional assumption, or necessarily self-evident. Axioms can be inconsistent. Choosing axioms is choosing a system.

common_meaning: Self-evident or unquestionable; relating to or based on axioms.
example: It is axiomatic that supply affects price.
rrgm_bridge: In its formal use, a statement of where something sits in a system. In its ordinary use, a claim that no argument is needed, which is a stronger thing to say.
invariant_mi: Having the standing of an axiom, or built by derivation from axioms.

domain_entries.FOR: Of a theory or method: proceeding from stated axioms by stated rules.
domain_entries.COG: Of a claim: taken as obvious.

count_condition: A system or a claim, and its axiom-like standing.
transfer_boundary: A formal axiom is a stipulation. Calling a claim about the world axiomatic does not support it and tends to close the question.

common_meaning: An imaginary line about which a body rotates; a reference line for measuring coordinates; a central line or structure; an alliance.
example: The Earth turns on its axis once a day.
rrgm_bridge: A comparison needs an axis. Naming it is the first step, and asking why that axis was chosen is a separate check.
invariant_mi: A line taken as the fixed reference about which things turn or along which they are ordered.

domain_entries.FOR: A coordinate reference line.
domain_entries.PHY: A line of rotation or symmetry.
domain_entries.BIO: A main line of the body plan; the second neck vertebra; a chain of interacting glands.
domain_entries.REL: An alignment between powers; a dimension along which positions are compared.

count_condition: A reference line, and things turning about it or ordered along it.
transfer_boundary: An axis is not an axle, which is a physical shaft. It is usually imaginary. Which axes are chosen determines which differences show.

inventory_review_note: Not found in SEARCH_INDEX_v1.5.tsv; check other addon lists before canonical insertion
common_meaning: In the study of religion and myth, the centre of the world conceived as a link between heaven, earth, and the underworld.
example: The world tree serves as an axis mundi in Norse myth.
rrgm_bridge: A centre from which orientation is taken, and the place where the realms are joined and so can be crossed.
invariant_mi: The centre of the world conceived as a vertical link joining the cosmic realms.

domain_entries.MYT: A comparative category applied to world trees, sacred mountains, and pillars in many traditions.
domain_entries.LIN: Latin for "axis of the world".

count_condition: A named tradition, a centre, and a connection between cosmic levels.
transfer_boundary: The term is a scholar's category; traditions use their own names. A tradition may have many such centres. Not every sacred centre is a vertical link.

common_meaning: A rod or shaft on which a wheel or pair of wheels turns.
example: The cart broke an axle on the track.
rrgm_bridge: The physical shaft, where "axis" is the line.
